decision: closed_no_credit: The reviewed research does not establish a qualifying benefit for this product's assessed use.
summary: The reviewed research does not establish a qualifying benefit for this product's assessed use. 29599478 (24 healthy adults aged 55-79, NIAGEN 1000 mg/day for 6 weeks) met its primary objective of raising PBMC NAD+ (~60%), which is verified target engagement, but blood-pressure and other physiological findings were exploratory and not significant after correction. 29992272 (40 obese men, 2000 mg/day for 12 weeks) found no improvement in insulin sensitivity, glucose metabolism or body composition. Under Dr. Pham's principle that a blood-marker-only result earns no clinical credit, the record becomes reference-only (completed, no applicable qualifying clinical support), which removes Evidence points from NIAGEN products.

population.description: 30 healthy, lean (mean BMI 24) men and women aged 55-79 randomized; 24 completed both phases.

study_contexts.study_design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 2x6-week crossover trial (NCT02921659); physiological outcomes prespecified as exploratory with one-sided tests and alpha 0.006.

outcomes.name: Primary objective: PBMC NAD+ rose ~60% versus placebo (mean change 6.2 pmol/mg protein; one-sided 95% CI 0.074 to infinity): verified target engagement
Exploratory: systolic BP -3.9 mmHg and diastolic BP -2.0 mmHg, not significant after correction for multiple comparisons
Tolerability: no serious adverse events; 14 treatment-emergent adverse events in 7 of 30 participants

limitations: Dr. Pham's principle (2026-10-28 rulings): a blood-marker-only result earns no clinical credit. The NAD+ rise is verified target engagement, not a demonstrated health benefit.
Small (24 completers), short (6 weeks per phase) crossover in healthy older adults; blood-pressure and arterial-stiffness signals are hypothesis-generating only.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

population.description: 40 healthy, sedentary men aged 40-70 with BMI >30 kg/m2 (obese, insulin-resistant).

study_contexts.study_design: Investigator-initiated randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind parallel-group trial (NCT02303483), 12 weeks; hyperinsulinemic euglycemic clamp, tracers, DXA, MRI/MRS.

outcomes.name: Insulin sensitivity, endogenous glucose production, glucose disposal and oxidation: not improved by NR
Resting energy expenditure, lipolysis, lipid oxidation and body composition: no effect; no serious adverse events

limitations: Full text not open access to this session (publisher PDF blocked); abstract only. Primary-outcome designation and NAD+ measurements were not verifiable here.
Men only; obese and insulin-resistant population.
